events.event: ABHI Microfinance Bank raised over Rs. 2 billion through the book-building portion of its IPO on the Pakistan Stock Exchange.
events.source_excerpt:
ABHI Microfinance Bank has raised about Rs. 2.05 billion through the book-building portion of its IPO, after demand ran past the shares on offer, according to Pakistan Stock Exchange book-building data and a company announcement.
The book-building tranche covered 99 million of the bank’s 132 million ordinary shares on offer, at a floor price of Rs. 15.00.
PSX data show an indicative strike price of Rs. 15.50, with bids for about 157.17 million shares, which is roughly 159 percent of the offer at the floor and about 106% at the strike.
The company said the book build is Pakistan’s first fintech-led microfinance bank IPO. It reported bids of more than Rs. 2.4 billion, with strong interest from foreign funds, local institutions, and high-net-worth investors.
The remaining 33 million shares will go to the public at the strike price on November 12 and 13, 2026.
ABHI had earlier said the full IPO could raise between Rs. 2 billion and Rs. 3 billion, with proceeds meant to expand its loan book and strengthen its capital base. ProPakistani covered that plan in an earlier report.

events.event: The Pakistani government announced the fifth consecutive reduction in fuel prices, cutting petrol by Rs6.59 and high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 per litre.
events.source_excerpt:
The government on Friday once again decreased the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25, in the fifth consecutive cut in fuel prices.
Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs346 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs378.
The prices are applicable from Nov 7 (Saturday) to Nov 10 (Tuesday) due to a public holiday on Nov 9, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).
The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.
Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.
Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
Rise in fuel prices
The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.
The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.
Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.
On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

events.event: US President Donald Trump announced that Stephen Miller will become the next White House chief of staff.
events.source_excerpt:
President Donald Trump on Friday announced that Stephen Miller, one of his most powerful and politically aggressive aides, would be his next White House chief of staff following disastrous results for Republicans in the midterm elections.
Miller, whose titles until now were deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser, has orchestrated the most polarizing policies of Trump’s second term—most notably a brutal crackdown on immigration that has claimed the lives of US citizens.
Trump made the change public in a statement on his Truth Social platform, writing that Miller would take over from Susie Wiles on Monday—less than a week after Republicans lost the House and Senate in a searing rebuke of Trump’s policy agenda.
In recent days, Trump has privately blamed Wiles for the worst Republican midterm performance in decades, according to two sources familiar with the matter. Wiles submitted her resignation on Thursday, the sources say.
Trump broadly considered three candidates to replace Wiles, the sources say: special envoy Steve Witkoff, director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, and Miller.
But with the looming threat of congressional investigations starting next year, Trump settled on Miller, seemingly because of his zeal in defending the president and his deep loyalty. Miller has been with Trump since his first campaign and stood by him through his political exile in 2021.
Miller had made his interest for the job known inside the West Wing for weeks, ever since Wiles weathered a series of negative stories before the midterms that suggested her job was at risk, the sources say.

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is said to be weighing whether to resume large-scale strikes against Iran after Democrats’ sweeping victory in recent midterm elections, even as he opened a new diplomatic channel on Friday by calling Qatar’s emir to discuss efforts to end the eight-month-old conflict.
The call with Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani came amid an intensifying regional diplomatic effort to prevent another round of major hostilities. But Trump has continued to keep military action on the table, saying on Thursday that the world would “know very soon” whether he would make a deal with Tehran or order new strikes to “destroy what is left” of the country.
“I would prefer not to destroy what is left of the country, if possible, but I may have to do so,” Trump told reporters, adding that Iran could take 25 years to rebuild from the damage already inflicted.
Friday’s conversation with the Qatari leader focused on diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions. Sheikh Tamim’s office said he had emphasised dialogue and diplomatic means to resolve disputes and prevent further escalation.
Qatar has been playing a key intermediary role in efforts to negotiate an agreement between Washington and Tehran.
Trump’s latest moves illustrate the dilemma confronting him after the Republican party’s midterm debacle. Democrats have won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, giving them an opportunity to challenge his policies during the final two years of his presidency.

ISLAMABAD: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has agreed to extend electricity subsidies for protected consumers using up to 200 units per month for another six months, sources said on Saturday.
According to sources, the understanding was reached during negotiations between Pakistan and the IMF last month, following the government’s efforts to provide further relief to consumers on the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
Under the proposed arrangement, the subsidy on electricity consumption of up to 200 units, scheduled to end on December 31, 2026, may now remain in place until June 30, 2027.
This means the government could delay the withdrawal of the subsidy to July 1, 2027.

events.event: Pakistan's National CERT has issued an advisory warning banks and critical infrastructure operators about surging AI-powered cyber threats.
events.source_excerpt:
National CERT Warns of AI-Powered Cyberattacks on Banks and Critical Infrastructure
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (National CERT) has warned of growing cyberattacks from artificial intelligence (AI)-powered attacks targeting banks, financial institutions, and critical national infrastructure.
According to the advisory, cybercriminals could use AI technology to automate attacks, identify system vulnerabilities and launch coordinated cyber operations.
The warning highlights the potential risks to the banking sector, particularly core banking systems, digital banking platforms and online payment services.
National CERT Warns of AI-Powered Cyberattacks on Banks and Critical Infrastructure
National CERT has warned that AI-powered cyberattacks could allow attackers to manipulate the account balances displayed to bank customers. Such activities could create confusion and spread panic among customers about the reliability and security of the financial system.
Cybercriminals could also use AI to identify weaknesses in banking networks and exploit them through automated attacks.
The advisory identifies several warning signs that financial institutions should monitor. These include an increase in automated login attempts, unusual financial transactions and suspicious API activity.
National CERT has advised banks and financial institutions to strengthen their security arrangements. It has particularly recommended implementing multi-factor authentication (MFA) and improving the protection of banking systems.
Critical National Infrastructure Also at Risk
The warning also covers essential national infrastructure, including oil and gas facilities, power plants, water supply networks and industrial systems.

events.event: Severe smog has hit central and southern Punjab, with Multan recording an Air Quality Index of 492.
events.source_excerpt:
Bad air quality affects Punjab with beginning of the winter
- By Web Desk -
- Nov 07, 2026
LAHORE: Bad air quality keeps haunting the central and southern parts of Punjab on Saturday as Multan becomes the most polluted city of Pakistan, as per the Air Quality Index (AQI).
Multan’s AQI recorded 492 today, while air quality at Raiwind recorded 316. The AQI at Rahim Yar Khan recorded 304, in Faisalabad 287 and in Lahore 273.
Indian capital city New Delhi ranked first among the most polluted cities of the world with the particulate matter’s level at the Air Quality Index recorded 539 today.
The air pollution and smog haunts Punjab with the onset of the winter. In previous years authorities made desperate efforts to contain smog in cities. The province grappled with severe air pollution, which soared to alarming levels, causing serious public health issues.
For days, Lahore was enveloped by smog, a mix of fog and pollutants, caused by low-grade diesel fumes, smoke from seasonal agricultural burning as temperatures drop with cooling air.
Air pollution level in Lahore once soared to more than 80 times of the level deemed hygienic by the World Health Organization (WHO).
The government closed schools and restricted timing of eateries, other businesses and markets to save general public from the adverse impact of toxic pollution and health problems.

events.event: The Sindh government officially declared Tharparkar a calamity-hit district and ordered emergency measures due to severe drought conditions.
events.source_excerpt:
Published November 07, 2026
KARACHI: The Sindh government has decided to officially declare Tharparkar a calamity-hit district amid drought-like conditions across the region.
The decision was taken during a meeting chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, who also directed the authorities to take immediate measures to address the situation in Tharparkar.
The briefing informed the chief minister that all seven talukas of Tharparkar were facing drought-like conditions, with between 85% and 90% of crops either destroyed or rendered unproductive.
According to the briefing, the agriculture extension department estimated crop losses at around 90%, while uneven rainfall had caused crops and natural grass to dry up before reaching maturity.
The chief minister was told that rainfall recorded across Tharparkar's seven talukas in September 2026 ranged from just one millimetre to 36 millimetres.
CM Murad directed the authorities to ensure the provision of drinking water to the people of Tharparkar and ordered the immediate repair and restoration of inactive reverse osmosis plants.
He also directed that all existing sources of water supply be restored without delay.
The chief minister instructed the chief secretary to examine the feasibility of laying a water pipeline from Naukot to Mithi and undertake long-term planning for water supply to the area.
He further sought recommendations on measures that could be taken to support livestock affected by the drought.
CM Murad directed continuous monitoring of relief measures in drought-affected areas, saying the Sindh government would not leave the affected people of Tharparkar alone and would provide every possible assistance.

original_source.name: Geo News
original_source.basis: Official briefing and decision chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah.

events.source_excerpt:

The operation was carried out under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, which aims to eliminate Fitna al-Khawarij and establish lasting peace in the province.
Reports quoted security sources that troops recovered a cache of weapons and ammunition from the terrorists killed during the operation.
Clearance operations are continuing in the area to search for and eliminate any other terrorists who may be present, the sources said.
Pakistan has witnessed a rise in terrorist attacks, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.
The country recorded its highest monthly number of terrorist attacks in 12 years in September 2026.
Islamabad has repeatedly called on Kabul to prevent terrorist organisations from using Afghan territory to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.
Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban government has failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.

According to the document, “Bushra Bibi was wearing exceptionally dark sunglasses. When she removed them at the insistence of Imran Khan and myself, she appeared immensely distressed.”
Barrister Safdar stated in the affidavit that “Bushra Bibi informed me she can tolerate neither sunlight nor artificial light.”

Safdar noted in his affidavit: “I observed that her eyesight has been severely affected, while Imran Khan also appeared deeply concerned over her deteriorating condition. The counsel added that “Bushra Bibi expressed dissatisfaction with the sanitary conditions in jail as well as her medical treatment, demanding examination and treatment by her private doctors.”

events.event: Pakistani oil refineries face negative refining margins as international petrol prices fell below crude oil prices.
events.source_excerpt:
Pakistan’s oil refineries are facing fresh financial pressure as international petrol prices have fallen below crude oil prices, pushing refining margins into negative territory for the first time in recent history.
According to Topline Research, petrol refining margins dropped to negative $1 per barrel on a seven-day rolling average basis as of November 6. International petrol prices stood at $105.90 per barrel, compared with Dubai crude oil at $106.90 per barrel. On November 5, the daily refining margin fell further to negative $5 per barrel.
The decline became visible in international price data compiled by OGRA and Topline Research. Petrol and Dubai crude prices moved relatively closely throughout much of October before falling sharply towards the end of the month. By November 5, petrol prices had dropped below crude oil prices, putting additional pressure on refinery profitability.
Refining margins, also known as cracks, represent the difference between the selling price of refined petroleum products and the cost of crude oil used to produce them. When petrol prices fall below crude oil prices, refiners face losses on petrol production.
The situation has become more challenging for domestic refineries following the imposition of a Rs. 49 per litre levy on petrol. The combination of negative international refining margins and the additional domestic levy is expected to further squeeze the profitability of Pakistan’s refining sector.
The latest development adds to the financial challenges facing local refineries as international fuel prices and domestic levies continue to affect their operating margins.

original_source.basis: Analysis based on industry data and research reports.

A report issued by Rescue 1122 stated that around 12:30am on Nov 7 an 11KVA electricity line passing over a house in Chak 272/HR snapped and fell on three individuals inside, killing them instantly.
The victims were identified as 40-year-old Muhammad Boota, his wife Shazia (35), and son Salman (15).
Fort Abbas SHO Adnan Ali told Dawn that the three-member family worked at a brick kiln and lived in a small, makeshift house.
He said that in the early hours of Saturday, the power line fell on Salman, who was asleep in the courtyard. Hearing his hue and cry, his parents, who were sleeping inside a room, tried to rescue him and they were also electrocuted and killed on the spot.
Meanwhile, locals said that high-voltage cables were dilapidated and had been repaired in many areas and complaints had been made several times to the local Mepco officials. However, they claimed that no action had been taken in this regard, resulting in this tragedy.
They urged that the negligent Mepco officials be held accountable through a transparent investigation.
When contacted, Mepco Bahawalnagar Superintending Engineer (SE) Khalid Sial claimed that no cable was broken or repaired and said that Multan-based investigation teams were on their way to the location to look into the matter.

Iran says two tankers caught fire in Hormuz after hitting mines
- By AFP -
- Nov 08, 2026
TEHRAN: Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday, according to state news agency IRNA.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
“Two oil tankers violating regulations — one in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the strait — caught fire and are currently engulfed in intense flames after striking naval mines while attempting to cross through unauthorised routes,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement.
“The two tankers had reportedly committed multiple violations, including switching off their navigation and positioning systems, as they attempted to transit through an unauthorised route,” the statement added.
The Guards did not specify the name or nationality of the tankers.
Tehran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying that ships have caught fire in the Hormuz strait.
US Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.
The IRNA separately reported late on Saturday that sounds of explosions were heard in parts of the country.

events.source_excerpt:
Vaccinate children: Today is the last day of sub-national anti polio drive: NEOC
- By Jahangir Khan -
- Nov 08, 2026
ISLAMABAD: The National Emergency Operation Centre (NEOC) for Polio on Sunday announced that today is the final day of a week-long sub-national anti-polio drive conducted across 97 selected districts, ARY News reported.
The NEOC stated that more than 20.38 million children have been administered polio drops over the past six days, against an overall target of 20.40 million.
A whopping 200,000 polio workers are participating in this vital drive across the country under tight security.
Meanwhile, the campaign was carried out simultaneously in both Pakistan and Afghanistan.
So far this year, nine polio cases have been reported across the country, showing that the risk of infection remains high.
Polio is untreatable and has no cure; vaccination is the only way to prevent the disease.
The NEOC has urged parents to fully cooperate with polio teams and immunize their children.
Parents should ensure that all children aged five and under receive drops during the ongoing door-to-door drive.
The NEOC also emphasized the importance of immunizing children against other preventable diseases.

events.event: Dawn's analysis examines how Pakistan's auto policy can better serve the general public rather than just high-income households.
events.source_excerpt:
For one woman interviewed for the 2019 social assessment of Karachi’s planned Yellow Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT), getting to her job destination meant walking 20 minutes to a road crossing, paying for a rickshaw and then paying again for a bus.
Other women interviewed for the assessment relied on shared three-wheelers that waited to fill up with passengers before leaving. For some, the journey could take two hours each way. Monthly transport costs ranged from Rs3,000 to Rs6,000 in households where incomes of Rs20,000 to Rs30,000 were common.
Fares can eat into an already modest wage. An unreliable connection can make a worker late. A second fare at each end of the journey can make studying at a college or a job across town too expensive a proposition to take up.
The draft for Pakistan’s Auto Policy 2026-31 revolves around car prices, manufacturers and tariffs. Yet, most households in the country own no car and struggle with the daily cost of commuting. Mobility for work, education and healthcare remains restricted due to unavailability of affordable and safe public transportation choices. How can Pakistan’s auto policy serve the people at large and not just the top decile of households in the country?
THE FAULT IN OUR DRAFTS
In April, when petrol rose by more than Rs137 a litre, governments briefly treated the price of a bus ticket as a cost-of-living issue. Islamabad announced 30 days of free public transport. events.event: The price of an 11.67kg household LPG cylinder in Pakistan surged to an all-time high of Rs6,498.
events.source_excerpt:
The price of a household liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinder in Pakistan has surged to an all-time high of Rs. 6,498, up nearly 80 percent since the beginning of 2026.
According to the latest available data as of November 5, the price of an 11.67kg cylinder has climbed sharply. This has added extra pressure on households that rely on LPG for cooking and heating.
The situation has been particularly difficult for households without access to piped natural gas, as well as those facing irregular gas supplies.
Pakistan has also faced disruptions in LPG imports following the closure of key border crossings with Iran in October. Iran accounts for a significant share of Pakistan’s LPG imports, and the disruption has tightened supplies in the domestic market.
LPG has recently been selling for as much as Rs. 500 per kg in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, while prices in some hilly areas have reached Rs. 600 per kg.
The difference between official and market prices has also become a big problem.
The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) set the official LPG price for November at Rs. 294.07 per kilogram, putting the notified price of an 11.8kg domestic cylinder at Rs. 3,470.09. However, consumers have been paying double in the retail market.
With winter approaching, higher demand for cooking and heating fuel could add further pressure on LPG supplies and household budgets.

events.event: Pakistan defeated India by three wickets in the Under-19 Asia Cup match, driven by Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten century.
events.source_excerpt:
Pakistan beat India in U19 Asia Cup after Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten century
- By Asim Mallick -
- Nov 08, 2026
Pakistan defeated arch-rivals India in the Under-19 Asia Cup after a brilliant unbeaten century by Hamza Zahoor helped the team chase down a 209-run target in a thrilling contest in Oman.
Pakistan were in serious trouble during the chase as their first five batters were dismissed for just 61 runs, putting India in a strong position to win the match.
However, batter Hamza Zahoor turned the game around with a match-winning performance, scoring an unbeaten 100 off 108 balls to guide Pakistan to victory.
Hamza, who came in at number seven, smashed three sixes and 10 fours during his innings, taking the game away from India and helping Pakistan complete a memorable win.
He was supported by Hasnain Abbas Dar, who scored 38 off 67 balls. The pair put together a crucial 107-run partnership for the sixth wicket to bring Pakistan back into the contest and put the team on course for victory.
Earlier, India were bowled out for 208 in the 47th over after batting first.

WHEN COP31 opens in Antalya today, governments will have to show that years of climate negotiations have produced more than ambitious targets and promises of financial help. Geopolitical tensions, an energy crisis, and strained finances in rich countries have dampened hopes of a breakthrough. The absence of an official US delegation after Washington’s withdrawal from the Paris Agreement has worsened matters.
Meanwhile, the climate crisis is advancing faster than efforts to contain it. A new UN report warns that even if countries fulfil existing climate pledges, global temperatures could rise by 2.6°C this century.
For Pakistan, already exposed to floods, extreme heat, and erratic rainfall, the question is what it can realistically secure from the talks.
At COP29, developed countries committed to mobilising $300bn annually for developing nations by 2035. COP30 called for progress towards a broader goal of $1.3tr a year and for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035. But promises of more money mean little if vulnerable states cannot access it.
For Pakistan, the priority should be to secure easier access to climate funds, more grants rather than debt-creating loans, and clear deadlines for financial contributions. It should seek support for practical measures to protect homes from flooding, secure water supplies, and improve early warning systems. By joining forces with other vulnerable countries, Pakistan could strengthen calls for better glacier monitoring, flood protection, and affordable climate technology.

ISLAMABAD: Increasingly frequent and severe heatwaves in Punjab’s rain-fed rural areas are disrupting agricultural production, reducing household incomes and worsening food insecurity, particularly among women and vulnerable communities, according to a report by United Nations (UN) agencies.
The assessment “Extreme Heat and Agriculture”, was published jointly by the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
It warns that rising temperatures have emerged as one of the most serious and acute hazards facing global food production, threatening the livelihoods of billions of people while inflicting immediate economic and nutritional damage on vulnerable farming communities.
“The effects of extreme heat on production are stark, as heat waves have led to significant declines in crop yields,” the report said.
In the high-rainfall zones of Punjab, fruit productivity has fallen by as much as 50 per cent, the agencies found.

events.event: Financial analysts report that overseas Pakistanis' remittances have reached $44 billion on a trailing 12-month basis, covering external deficits and accounting for about 10 percent of GDP.
events.source_excerpt:
Remittances from overseas Pakistanis now cover 100 percent of the external deficits of the country and account for about 10 percent of GDP, according to Emre Akcakmak, Head of Frontier Markets and portfolio advisor at East Capital.
Akcakmak said on Tuesday that remittances have reached $44 billion on a trailing 12-month basis, one of the highest levels relative to GDP globally. In a post on X, he said the economy would be in a completely different shape without the inflows from an estimated 10 million Pakistanis living abroad.
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data released the same day supports the trend. Remittances sent by Workers totalled $3.9 billion in October, up 14 percent from $3.42 billion a year earlier and 8.5 percent higher than $3.6 billion in September.
Cumulative inflows for July-October FY27 rose 14 percent to $14.8 billion, compared with $13 billion in the same period last year. Last month, the SBP raised its FY27 remittance forecast to $45 billion from $44 billion, citing resilient inflows in the first quarter.
Akcakmak contrasted the current position with the year 2023, when Pakistan nearly defaulted on its foreign currency bonds. External deficits had widened sharply, and central bank reserves covered only 1.5 months of imports.
Since then, gross foreign exchange reserves have risen almost fivefold. Inflation has fallen from 38 percent to single digits, with a low of 0.2 percent and a latest reading of 9.6 percent. Equities have gained 318 percent in US dollar terms, or 53 percent annualised.
Akcakmak credited the diaspora for the turnaround, alongside a stable government and an effective IMF programme. He described remittances as “Pakistan’s oil.”

events.event: Around 85,000 people left Karachi for employment abroad between January and September, consisting largely of laborers, drivers, and skilled professionals.
events.source_excerpt:
Some 85,000 people left Karachi for employment abroad between January and September 30 this year, with professionals from 63 occupations among them, according to available figures.
Laborers and support staff made up the largest group, at 32,626 people. Drivers followed with 20,556, and general workers came third with 20,332. Together, these three categories account for more than 73,000 of the total.
Skilled professionals also left in significant numbers. The figures show 560 doctors, 526 accountants, 298 computer programmers, 233 financial analysts, 260 teachers, 145 systems analysts, 96 nurses, 43 pharmacists and six pilots went abroad.
Aircraft technicians, budget controllers, designers, managers and X-ray technicians also departed in notable numbers. Monthly figures show departures were comparatively higher in January, February, July and September.
In October, the Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment released data showing that a total of 66,815 Pakistanis had left the country for employment over the previous two months.
The report showed that 27,656 Pakistanis went abroad in search of work in August 2026, compared with 39,159 in July. The number of overseas workers fell by 11,503 month-on-month.

Pakistan’s federal government has collected nearly Rs. 35 billion from the four provinces by deducting the amount from their shares under the National Finance Commission (NFC) award, marking the first such deduction under Article 164 of the Constitution since the country’s creation.
Federal government received Rs. 34.839 billion from the provinces as grants during the first two months of the current fiscal year. The amount has been recorded as non-tax revenue in the government’s accounts.

The deductions follow an agreement reached between the federal government and all four provinces before the presentation of the 2026-27 federal budget. Under the arrangement, the provinces agreed to provide Rs. 1.035 trillion from their NFC shares during the fiscal year to help the federal government meet its financial obligations under the International Monetary Fund’s $7 billion loan program.
The latest collection represents part of the financial support committed by the provinces under the agreement.

events.event: The International Energy Agency reported that global oil supply exceeded demand in the fourth quarter for the first time since the war in Iran began.
events.source_excerpt:
Published November 13, 2026
Global oil supplies are expected to exceed demand in the fourth quarter, after increased Gulf exports led to a market surplus in October for the first time since the Iran war, the International Energy Agency said Friday.
Even though attacks on tankers trying to transit the Strait of Hormuz have continued, Gulf shipments reached 18.4 million barrels per day (mb/d) -- though that was still 26% below pre-war levels, the Paris-based agency said in its monthly report.
"The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran," the IEA said.
Prices have fallen sharply in recent weeks as more vessels prove willing to make the risky transit through the Strait of Hormuz under US escort.
Iran effectively closed the crucial strait in the early months of the war launched by the United States and Israel in late February.
That helped overall oil supply to rise by three million barrels per day in September and a further 2.3 million barrels in October, the IEA said.
But global demand is set to fall by 2.7 mb/d overall this year as oil prices remain well above pre-war levels and "accelerate electrification and fuel efficiencies across the global car fleet".
Diesel prices in particular stood at $180 per barrel in October, around 77% higher than before the war, as Iran struck refineries in neighbouring Gulf countries accused of aiding US attacks.
Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and other energy installations are also disrupting diesel supplies to the global market.
"The severe tightness in product supply, especially for diesel, remains the overriding concern of the broader market and consumers," the IEA said.

original_source.name: International Energy Agency
original_source.basis: Monthly report issued by the IEA in Paris.

events.event: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage affecting global communication and institutional tools dragged into a second day.
events.source_excerpt:
A dramatic Microsoft 365 outage impacting widely used services like Outlook, Teams, and Copilot dragged into a second day on Friday after the company failed overnight to resolve an issue that left institutions and individuals around the world without crucial communication tools. The services did seem to be on a slow path to recovery by midmorning on Friday.
“We’re observing sustained improvements in service availability,” Microsoft said in a statement posted to its status dashboard on Friday morning. The company had said on Thursday evening that its initial attempts to fix the problem were “not taking as expected.”
The outages have caused widespread disruption to schools, courts, governments, and law enforcement agencies—plus countless businesses and millions of employees—around the globe, highlighting how many of the world’s most crucial systems rely upon technologies from a small number of tech companies. And when they fail, the ramifications can be huge.
Microsoft has not said yet what caused the outage but has hinted that it was related to cascading server failures inside multiple data centers around the world that shifted too much load onto remaining operational machines.
“We determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure,” the company wrote in Microsoft 365 Status update on Thursday afternoon. “We’re testing a configuration change to address a problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable,” the company added a few minutes later.

events.event: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed two oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
events.source_excerpt:
Iran Guards say two oil tankers hit by mines in Hormuz
- By AFP -
- Nov 14, 2026
Tehran: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that explosions rang out on two oil tankers after they struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, where Tehran has restricted navigation.
Since war erupted with the United States in February, Tehran has insisted that vessels obtain its authorisation to cross the strait and has attacked ships that do not comply.
“A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorised route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine,” the Guards’ navy said in a statement carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday.
The statement did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but said one was a supertanker.
The United States, in response to Tehran’s choking of the strategic trade route, has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and provides military support to tankers using the waterway.
In recent weeks, Iran’s armed forces have reported several fires or explosions on board ships in the strait, often saying the vessels had struck mines.
On Friday, the Guards released footage of a large plume of smoke rising from a vessel it said was carrying liquefied gas and hit a mine in the south of the strait.
The US military, however, says it has cleared the main routes through the waterway of mines.

NADRA shares steps to recover existing Pak ID accounts online
- By Kumail Shah -
- Nov 14, 2026
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has shared steps for citizens to recover their Pak ID accounts if their CNIC numbers are already registered in the mobile app.
NADRA says that if users see an error saying their CNIC number is already linked to another account when registering on the Pak ID app, they should recover their existing account instead of making a new one.
To access their account, users should open the Pak ID app, enter their CNIC number on the login screen, and select the “Forgot Password” option. After that, they should enter their registered email address to receive a two-factor authentication (2FA) code.
Once users enter the verification code, they need to complete biometric verification to confirm their identity. After finishing these steps, they can access their Pak ID account.
The Pak ID app lets users access NADRA services like CNIC renewal, modification, replacement, and other identity-related applications. If citizens still have trouble logging in or registering, they can call NADRA’s helpline at 1777 for help.

original_source.name: NADRA
original_source.basis: NADRA shared recovery instructions via official channels and media.

events.event: A Lahore green bus conductor was fired after a video went viral showing him mistreating and pushing a female passenger.
events.source_excerpt:
Lahore green bus conductor fired for mistreating female passenger
- By Hamid Ur Rehman -
- Nov 14, 2026
LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Saturday shared a video of a bus conductor apologising after he allegedly misbehaved with a female passenger and pushed her off a Lahore Green Electric Bus.
The incident sparked outrage on social media after a video showing the conductor’s behaviour went viral, prompting citizens to demand strict action against those responsible.
Punjab Transport and Mass Transit Minister Bilal Akbar Khan took notice of the incident and ordered immediate action against the employee involved.
Responding to the incident, the minister said: “Thank you for bringing this matter to our attention. This is a serious act of misconduct. The conductor has been dismissed from his job. The Transport Department condemns his inappropriate behaviour and apologises for the incident. No one has the right to humiliate or mistreat another human being.”
Conductor Terminated by BRT Management
Following an internal review, the Lahore BRT management took disciplinary action against the conductor, identified as Ali Rizwan, and terminated his employment.
In its termination notice, the management stated that the incident involving a female passenger had been captured on video and subsequently reviewed by the company.
The review established that the employee had failed to handle the situation in accordance with the company’s passenger-handling standards, professional conduct requirements and Corporate Code of Conduct.
Consequently, the management decided to terminate his services on disciplinary grounds.
Maryam Nawaz Orders Arrest and Public Apology
However, Maryam Nawaz said that dismissing the conductor from his job was not sufficient and directed the police

events.event: Google is increasing the annual price of its Google One 30GB subscription plan in Pakistan by nearly 32% starting January 2027.
events.source_excerpt:
Google One 30GB Subscription Price to Increase by Nearly 32% in Pakistan
Google One subscribers in Pakistan may soon have to pay more for cloud storage. Google LLC is increasing the annual price of its Google One (30GB) plan from Rs 1,899 to Rs 2,500, effective January 12, 2027, for the notified subscription.
The move represents an increase of Rs 601 per year, or approximately 31.65%, making the entry-level cloud storage subscription considerably more expensive for affected users.
Google One 30GB Subscription: Old vs New Price
| Subscription | Current annual price | New annual price | Increase | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Google One (30GB) | Rs 1,899 | Rs 2,500 | Rs 601 (31.65%) | 
As per the notification, the revised price will take effect on January 12, 2027. On a monthly equivalent basis, the annual subscription cost will rise from around Rs 158 to Rs 208. These figures are calculated from the annual charges and do not represent a separate monthly subscription offer.
What Does the Price Hike Mean for Pakistani Users?
Google One provides additional cloud storage that can be used across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos. For users who regularly back up their photos, store documents online, or receive large email attachments, a paid storage subscription can be an important part of their digital routine.
However, the latest price revision adds to the cost of maintaining digital subscriptions in Pakistan. While the increase amounts to Rs 601 annually, it is significant in percentage terms, particularly for users who subscribe to multiple online services.
This is not the first time Google One pricing has changed. PhoneWorld has previously reported on Google One subscription price increases in Pakistan, as well as pricing revisions in other countries.
Can Users Avoid Paying

original_source.name: Google LLC / PhoneWorld
original_source.basis: Notification sent to subscribers regarding price revision.

events.event: Former Pakistan cricketer Wasim Akram questioned Australia captain Pat Cummins' denial of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
events.source_excerpt:
Pakistan pace legend Wasim Akram has questioned Australia captain Pat Cummins’ claim that he was unaware of the use of sandpaper during the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa, arguing that any experienced bowler would immediately recognise the difference between natural wear and deliberate damage to the ball.
Speaking in a video posted on social media on Saturday from Melbourne, Wasim said the marks left by sandpaper were distinctly different from those caused by normal contact with the ground.
“As a bowler, I’ll have a look at the ball and know straight away something is not right,” Wasim said.
“He said he didn’t know (about the use of sandpaper). As a bowler, when the cricket ball comes into my hand, whether it’s the fifth over, the tenth over or the fiftieth over, you look after the ball, you shine one side of the ball. But the sandpaper scratch is totally different than the one-bounce scratch.”
Wasim suggested that the difference could easily be identified through a simple comparison, saying anyone could take a semi-new ball, rub sandpaper against it and observe the resulting marks.
The former Pakistan captain, widely regarded as one of the finest exponents of reverse swing, described Cummins as “a very close friend” and insisted he was not taking sides in the controversy, which has resurfaced following revelations by former Australia opener Usman Khawaja in his autobiography Sabr.
Khawaja alleged that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was widespread within the Australian dressing room, including among the bowling group, during the 2018 tour of South Africa.

events.event: Police successfully foiled a terrorist attack on a checkpost in Bannu, eliminating four terrorists.
events.source_excerpt:
BANNU: Police foiled a terrorist attack on Kingar Pul Police Checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu district on Friday night, eliminating four terrorists in retaliation, a police spokesperson said.
According to the police spokesperson, heavily armed terrorists launched a sudden attack on the checkpost last night.
“However, police personnel deployed at the checkpost responded promptly and successfully repelled the assault,” he stated.
Following the incident, the Rapid Response Force (RRF) and additional police personnel were rushed from Police Lines to the scene. They cordoned off the area and launched a clearance and search operation, the spokesperson added.
“During the operation, the bodies of four terrorists were recovered,” he added.
The spokesperson said that police also seized four Kalashnikov rifles, several magazines, a substantial quantity of ammunition, hand grenades and bandoliers, adding that the identification of the slain terrorists was underway.
Meanwhile, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed commended Bannu Police for foiling the attack.
He said successfully repelling the assault under the cover of darkness reflected the high level of training, vigilance and bravery of police personnel.
The IG added that effective operations were underway under a comprehensive strategy to eliminate terrorism and rid the province of the menace.
“Protecting the lives and property of the public remains the top priority of the police,” IG Hameed said.

events.source_excerpt:
The Punjab Boards Committee of Chairpersons has announced the starting date for the 2027 matriculation examinations, giving students an early timeline to prepare for their annual papers.
According to an official notification issued on November 10, the SSC Part II first annual examinations will begin on March 16, 2027.
The Punjab Boards Committee of Chairpersons approved the schedule in anticipation of the committee’s formal approval, following a proposal from the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Lahore.
The announcement provides students across Punjab with a clear timeline for the upcoming matric examinations and allows them to plan their preparation accordingly. The notification also outlines the admission schedule for students who want to appear in the examinations.

events.source_excerpt:
Published November 14, 2026
Pakistan will host 30th Meeting of the ECO Council of Ministers in Islamabad on November 15-16 with an aim to strengthen regional connectivity and integration, said the Foreign Office on Saturday.
In a statement, the FO said the meeting will be chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and will be attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations of ECO member states, along with representatives of the ECO secretariat and its subsidiary bodies.
Iran, Turkiye, Azerbaijan, Afghanistan and five Central Asian republics are among the 10 member states of the ECO.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to attend the huddle in Islamabad amid ongoing Middle East conflict with mediators Pakistan and Qatar making efforts to broker peace deal between Iran and the US.
The Foreign Office further said that the ministerial meeting will be preceded by the Meeting of Senior Officials (SOM) of ECO Member States, which will review the activities and programmes of the organisation, assess the work of its subsidiary bodies, and finalise the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the ministers during COM.
As chair of the ECO for 2026-2027, Pakistan will seek to advance the Organisation's objectives under the theme "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO," it added.
Pakistan's chairmanship, the FO said, will focus on strengthening regional connectivity and deepening regional integration to strengthen regional partnerships, and promote collective efforts towards greater prosperity, sustainable development, and a more integrated and resilient ECO region.

events.event: The United States reopened its airspace and lifted a nationwide flight halt after an air traffic control communications failure, while officials sought billions in funding.
events.source_excerpt:
The United States (US) reopened its airspace on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centres forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to halt flights nationwide, disrupting thousands of journeys, while Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called on Congress to provide $50 billion in emergency funding to overhaul the country’s ageing air traffic control system.
The FAA lifted the nationwide ground stop allowing flights to resume. However, Duffy warned that airlines will take time to restore their operations and clear the backlog of disrupted journeys.
“It’s going to be slow,” Duffy told reporters at the White House.
According to FlightRadar24, more than 6,600 flights were cancelled and another 8,600 delayed following the disruption. Airlines had also cancelled 1,500 flights scheduled for Sunday. Aviation analysts said that the four-hour nationwide grounding could affect airline schedules for several days.
Duffy stated that tens of thousands of passengers remained stranded at airports across the country. He added that he and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had met President of US Donald Trump in the Oval Office to discuss the incident.
The disruption began when air traffic control centres experienced instability in their radar and communications systems. Duffy said that overloaded switches and routers caused inconsistencies in the data transmitted through the network, prompting officials to shut down the system.
“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data and they started to give us inconsistencies in the data from those routers and because of that we shut the system down,” he said.

events.source_excerpt:
US to resume flights after air traffic network failure sparks chaos
- By Reuters -
- Nov 14, 2026
WASHINGTON: The FAA lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centers caused chaos at US airports and triggered the longest shutdown since the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said US airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (0115 GMT), but warned that departures would resume gradually and it would take time for airlines to restore normal operations.
“It’s going to be slow,” Duffy told reporters at the White House.
By 11:30 p.m., nearly 10,000 flights had been canceled, including more than 2,200 each at Delta Air Lines and American Airlines, and 1,800 at United Airlines, according to Flightradar24.
The plane-tracking website said some aircraft at major airports had waited more than five hours for a gate.
The four-hour nationwide grounding could disrupt airline schedules for days, aviation analysts said.
Duffy said tens of thousands of passengers were stranded at airports around the country.
Duffy said he and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had met with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office to discuss the outage.
The failure is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers.
Duffy said the trouble began at 3:36 p.m., when air traffic control centers experienced instability in radar and communications systems.

events.event: Punjab authorities expanded a crackdown on illegal stubble burning with a new quick-response pollution squad as smog shrouds Lahore.
events.source_excerpt:
Published November 14, 2026
LAHORE: As smog again settles over large parts of South Asia, authorities in Punjab are widening a crackdown on illegal stubble burning they say is fuelling the region's annual pollution crisis.
On Thursday, officers of a new quick-response unit swung off their vehicles at a paddy field on the edge of Lahore. Smoke curled low over the stubble, and the crew had the fire under control within minutes, keeping it from adding to the haze over a city that Swiss group IQAir rated “very unhealthy” earlier this week.
Farmers in the region commonly set leftover rice residue alight after the October harvest, fuelling a toxic mix of industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust and construction dust that lingers under cold winter air, driving pollution to hazardous levels.
The unit is the first of its kind in Pakistan dedicated to fighting pollution, officials say, and it is one of the most visible steps in a campaign that Punjab officials claim is working.
Satellites have detected less burned area in India and Pakistan than the historical average at this point in the year, even as many locals in Pakistan say they struggle to notice improvements.
Silwat Saeed, chief of the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department in Punjab, said the government this year formed a 750-member force in 67 rapid-response units across major rice-growing districts.
Teams aim to reach reported field fires within 10 to 15 minutes. Officials also patrol paddy areas for signs of burning, while complaints can be lodged locally, said Ashfaq Hussain, a deputy director of the force. “We receive complaints through multiple channels and respond to them in the shortest possible time,” he said.

events.event: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defense agreement in Istanbul aimed at adopting a unified position against external attacks.
events.source_excerpt:
Turkey, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
- By AFP -
- Nov 14, 2026
Istanbul: Turkey and Qatar announced on Friday that they signed a mutual defence agreement, which they said was aimed at adopting a “unified position” in the face of an external attack.
The announcement came after Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul.
Erdogan had said the agreement would further strengthen ties between the regional allies, according to his office.
Qatar’s ruler travelled to Istanbul after attending the United Nations COP31 climate summit in southern Turkey.
“The two parties hailed the signing of the mutual defence agreement between Qatar and Turkey,” according to a joint statement carried by Qatar’s state news agency.
The agreement was “aimed at bolstering collective defence and achieving regional security and stability, as well as adopting a unified position in the face of any external armed attack targeting either or both parties”, the statement said.
“The two parties agreed to hold consultations on threats to their security… and to strengthen cooperation through joint military exercises, collaboration in the field of defence industries, and the exchange of personnel training.”
Erdogan’s office had earlier announced the agreement, without going into the details of its contents.

“A mutual defence agreement signed by Turkey and Qatar today will add a new dimension to the brotherly ties between the two countries,” Erdogan said during the meeting, according to the statement from his office.

events.event: Microsoft announced that its global services, including Outlook and Teams, have been fully restored after a day-long worldwide outage.
events.source_excerpt:
Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
- Published
Microsoft has said its services have been fully restored after a worldwide outage affected several of its tools, causing disruption.
The tech firm said early on Saturday morning that efforts to address the underlying problem had been completed and customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer be affected.
The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.
Microsoft apologised for the technical issue, which it said was introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and was not caused by a cyber-attack or an artificial intelligence agent.
Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers.
Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday.
By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America.
Services were beginning to recover by Friday afternoon UK time, nearly 24 hours after the issues first began to emerge.

events.event: The State Bank of Pakistan reported that Pakistan's domestic debt dropped by over Rs 1.6 trillion during the first quarter of the fiscal year.
events.source_excerpt:
Pakistan’s domestic debt recorded a quarterly decline of Rs. 1.636 trillion in July to September, bringing the outstanding stock down to Rs. 57.757 trillion by the end of September.
The State Bank of Pakistan reported that domestic debt had stood at Rs. 59.393 trillion at the close of the previous fiscal year on June 30, indicating a significant reversal in the government’s borrowing pattern during the opening months of FY27.
Govt Steps Up Debt Repayments
State Bank data showed that the government’s net retirement of scheduled bank debt reached Rs. 1.847 trillion during July to October FY27, compared with Rs. 45 billion in the corresponding period last year. This indicates that repayments exceeded fresh borrowing during the period.
Borrowing through long-term Pakistan Investment Bonds (PIBs) declined by Rs. 1.756 trillion to Rs. 33.543 trillion by the end of September. The government has traditionally emphasized long-term bonds over short-term borrowing.
Treasury Bill Borrowing Declines
The government’s borrowing through short-term Treasury bills also fell by Rs. 1.163 trillion to Rs. 9.640 trillion during the first quarter of FY27, indicating a broader reduction in domestic borrowing across different debt instruments.
The decline comes as government revenues have increased and fiscal consolidation efforts have intensified under Pakistan’s International Monetary Fund (IMF) program. The government is seeking to further reduce its fiscal deficit during the current fiscal year.
Planning, Development and Special Initiative Minister Ahsan Iqbal recently said Pakistan’s fiscal deficit narrowed to 2.6 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in FY26, compared with 5.4 percent in FY25. He described it as the lowest fiscal deficit recorded in two decades.

events.event: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority is considering reducing the voice SIM card limit from five to three per CNIC to curb illegal activities.
events.source_excerpt:
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) is considering reducing the maximum number of voice SIM cards allowed against a single Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC) from five to three. The authority is also planning to increase the permissible limit for data SIMs to meet growing connectivity demands, particularly following the introduction of 5G services.
According to PTA officials, the proposed changes aim to prevent the misuse of multiple voice SIMs in cybercrimes and other illegal activities. Officials noted that most mobile phone users generally operate two to three voice SIMs, making the existing limit of five relatively high.
Meanwhile, the PTA is considering increasing the current limit of three data SIMs per CNIC to support growing demand for internet connectivity and Internet of Things (IoT) applications. The expansion of 5G services is also expected to increase the need for additional data connections.
The proposed changes will be finalised after consultations with mobile network operators. Currently, a maximum of eight SIMs can be registered against one CNIC, including five voice SIMs and three data SIMs.

original_source.basis: Reports citing PTA officials discussing proposed regulatory changes.

events.event: Former Gulistan-i-Jauhar SHO Kamran Qureshi was dismissed from service over misconduct and mishandling of evidence in the Mir Raza Ali murder case.
events.source_excerpt:
Former Gulistan-i-Jauhar station house officer (SHO), Kamran Qureshi, was dismissed from service on Saturday over charges of misconduct in the Mir Raza Ali murder case.
Last month, a joint investigation team (JIT) constituted by the Sindh government recommended an inquiry against Qureshi, who was suspended from duty, over the possible facilitation of the destruction of evidence.
According to the dismissal order seen by Dawn, Qureshi failed to secure the crime scene where Ali’s body was found and did not call in the Crime Scene Unit (CSU) as per regulations.
“As a result, the crime scene could not be processed promptly, which caused [a] delay in forensic examination and possible loss of important circumstantial evidence which [is] tantamount to gross misconduct, inefficiency [and] dereliction of duty. Thus, you have rendered yourself liable to be awarded one of the major punishment[s] under the Sindh Police (E&D) Rules, 1988,“ the order read.
The order further noted that an inquiry was conducted by Central Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Muhammad Imran Khan, who observed that Qureshi not only failed to discharge his duties in securing the crime scene and evidence, but did not even visit the site. The Central SSP recommended major punishment.
The order said that Qureshi also failed to submit a reply to a show-cause notice.
“He was called in [the] orderly room and heard in person on Nov 13. His oral explanation has been considered and found unsatisfactory, as he could not add any cogent reason to repudiate the allegations levelled against him,” the order read.
“Therefore, agreeing with the recommendation of [the] inquiry officer, he is hereby awarded major punishment of dismissal from service,” the order said.

events.event: Microsoft has fully restored services for Outlook, Teams, and other cloud applications following a massive global outage affecting multiple countries.
events.source_excerpt:
Tech giant Microsoft said on Saturday it has “restored service” to customers, effectively drawing a close to a massive outage that caused chaos and disrupted public services and business around the world.
“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the US-based company said in an X post.
Microsoft had already reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services the day before, stating the major disruption was due to a technical issue and “not related to cyber or AI/agents”.
The outage swept the globe on Thursday, taking the company’s products offline in at least 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.
Microsoft had attributed the disruption to “elevated load” on its infrastructure.
It said the stoppage affected its Outlook email service, as well as Microsoft’s Teams communication platform and the company’s Copilot AI assistant.
Microsoft on Friday apologised for the global outage as it reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services.
The company ruled out any malicious “cyber or AI” activity as the cause of the outage, which affected several Microsoft products and disrupted health care services, delayed corporate earnings reports and left schools struggling to communicate.
“We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” Microsoft said on X, adding that full services were still being restored after the outage started on Thursday.

original_source.basis: Official status post confirming full restoration of services.

events.source_excerpt:

- By Web Desk -

Pakistan produced a disciplined performance to beat hosts Bangladesh 1-0 and reach the SAFF Championship final, where they will face arch-rivals India.

events.event: Pakistan's domestic debt declined by Rs 1.636 trillion during the first quarter of FY27 to stand at Rs 57.757 trillion.
events.source_excerpt:
Pakistan’s domestic debt declined by Rs. 1.636 trillion during the first quarter of FY27, bringing the total outstanding debt to Rs. 57.757 trillion by the end of September 2026.
According to State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data, domestic debt stood at Rs. 59.393 trillion on June 30, marking a significant reduction in government borrowing during July-September.
The government also stepped up debt repayments, with net retirement of scheduled bank debt reaching Rs. 1.847 trillion during July-October FY27, compared with Rs. 45 billion in the same period last year. Borrowing through Pakistan Investment Bonds (PIBs) declined by Rs. 1.756 trillion to Rs. 33.543 trillion, while Treasury bill borrowing fell by Rs. 1.163 trillion to Rs. 9.640 trillion.
The decline comes amid higher government revenues and fiscal consolidation efforts under Pakistan’s International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal recently said the fiscal deficit narrowed to 2.6% of GDP in FY26, compared with 5.4% in FY25.
Despite the quarterly decline, domestic debt increased by Rs. 4.331 trillion over the 12 months ending September 2026. Meanwhile, external debt rose by Rs. 700 billion in rupee terms, reaching Rs. 24.9 trillion by the end of September.

events.event: A technical glitch disrupted a US press conference addressing nationwide flight disruptions caused by aging technology.
events.source_excerpt:
Trump administration officials were left red-faced on Saturday when their public effort to address the massive tech disruption that grounded thousands of US flights was itself hit with embarrassing technical glitches.
Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy took the podium and began addressing a much-anticipated and televised press conference a day after a disastrous nationwide ground stop across US airspace — one blamed on ageing technology — when a deep, echoing hum began to emanate from the microphones and speakers.
“Check one two, three four, five six seven?” Duffy said into the mic.
As cameras rolled, he paused, looked around, and stepped away.
“[I] apologise for that,” he said, as technicians scrambled to replace microphones and adjust cables.
Duffy soon resumed, but brittle feedback hit the room seconds later and his demeanour shifted, presumably all-too-aware that the symbolism of an on-camera tech meltdown after such a major flight disruption was not going unnoticed.
“This is not operational? OK,” said Duffy, appearing deeply irritated.
“This is our kind of, uh, day.”
Duffy was speaking to reporters with the head of the Federal Aviation Administration, Bryan Bedford, and, ironically, with the FAA’s chief technology officer Rebecca Guy, who he said was doing a press conference with him for the first time.
Duffy and Bedford repeatedly pointed to ongoing systemic issues with transitioning from ageing air traffic control technology from the 1970s and 1980s to more modern equipment.
As technicians scrambled, US networks carried the awkward pause — lasting an excruciating three minutes — live on the air.

original_source.name: Dawn
original_source.basis: Reported live from the US Department of Transportation press briefing.

- By Reuters -

Italy’s data protection agency said on Saturday it had fined Meta Platforms €805 million ($887 million) after finding the company had accessed Android users’ photographs and videos without obtaining their consent or informing them.
Meta had access to Android users’ photos and videos through a Facebook app feature that suggested content from users’ personal galleries that they could post, the authority said in a statement
Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users’ consent separately, it said

The authority also said that it had reserved the right to assess separately a new feature, launched in 2026, that allows content from users’ galleries to be processed in the cloud
The fine is equivalent to about 0.47% of the group’s global revenue, the authority said

events.event: China has successfully completed the maiden crewed flight of its indigenously developed all-electric passenger aircraft, the CE-25A, in Shandong province.
events.source_excerpt:
Published November 14, 2026
China's indigenously developed 10-tonne all-electric passenger aircraft, dubbed CE-25A, successfully completed its maiden crewed flight on Saturday, November 14, in the eastern province of Shandong.
The aircraft, carrying two pilots and a flight-test engineer, remained airborne for 16 minutes and 38 seconds, covering a distance of 60.4 kilometres.
Interestingly, the aircraft had already completed 19 autonomous flight tests before humans stepped inside its cockpit for a flight.
Developed by the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC) in collaboration with battery manufacturing giant CATL and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, the aircraft is designed to transport 19 passengers between cities.
Unlike conventional passenger planes, the CE-25A features 10 electrically powered ducted fans, five mounted on each wing.
The aircraft boasts a proposed range of 400 kilometres, a cruising speed of 300 kilometres per hour and a cruising altitude of 2,400 metres.
Its autonomous flight systems allow pilots to monitor operations and intervene whenever necessary.
The aircraft produces no direct carbon emissions during flight, potentially making short-distance air travel more environmentally friendly.
Meanwhile, the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) has accepted COMAC's application for the aircraft's type certification.
However, the manufacturer has yet to announce when passengers will be able to board the battery-powered aircraft for commercial flights.

SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket on its return to Earth for the first time.
"Can you believe it?," a commentator said as large crowds cheered at the launch site in Texas.
The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower.

The chain of events that ended Jensen Huang’s 33-year run as Nvidia CEO was set in motion by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, according to The Washington Post.

Huang had close ties with Trump and pushed hard for chip sales to China. In December 2025, Trump approved sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China in exchange for a share of the revenue. Many national security officials saw such sales as a threat.
His exit could now help lawmakers push three measures in a major defense bill: restricting exports of powerful AI chips, requiring technology to detect chip smuggling, and limiting China’s access to chipmaking equipment.
Trump, however, still publicly backs Huang, calling him a “legend” who had “done a fantastic job.” Huang’s troubles began with reports of his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

events.event: The Supreme Court has ruled that an inheritance-share suit becomes time-barred only if the defendant proves the claimant knew of the denial more than six years prior.

Likewise, if the heir is instead trying to cancel a document he himself was party to, the suit is late only if the defendant proves the heir knew of the grounds to cancel it more than three years before filing, says the SC while affirming that limitation in inheritance suits begins only when an heir learns of an overt act repudiating their title, not from the date of an incorrect revenue mutation or mere silence or passage of time.
“Time does not run against the heir; it runs against the heir’s knowledge of a wrong. The right of an heir, vested at the moment of death, never lapses with time,” observed Justice Shahid Waheed in a 106-page judgement authored by him.

events.event: The State Bank of Pakistan clarified that it cannot force merchants and stores to accept smartphone-based contactless payments as they are not directly regulated by the central bank.
events.source_excerpt:
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) cannot force shops and superstores like Metro to accept contactless payments made through smartphones, smartwatches and other wearable devices, as merchants are not directly regulated by it.
SBP informed ProPakistani that it does not regulate merchants and cannot direct them to accept any particular payment method.
Several shops have stopped accepting or restricted NFC payments made through digital devices, creating a grey area over whether retailers can refuse phone-based payments but continue accepting contactless debit and credit cards.
This means the central bank cannot compel sellers to restore phone-based contactless payments or require other them to support a specific digital payment method.
Who Is Responsible if a Contactless Payment Is Fraudulent?
The central bank has clarified how liability is determined when a PIN-free contactless payment is disputed as fraudulent.
Payment schemes such as Visa, Mastercard and PayPak have dedicated liability and dispute-resolution frameworks covering customers, merchants and acquiring banks.
Responsibility is determined on a case-by-case basis, depending on the actions, omissions or negligence of the parties involved.
This means liability is not automatically assigned to the customer or merchant whenever a contactless transaction is disputed.
SBP said these payment-scheme rules contain detailed provisions governing the rights and responsibilities of all parties and are designed to protect customers.
SBP Confirms Rs. 3,000 Limit for PIN-Free Payments
The central bank has also settled a question over the maximum amount allowed for contactless transactions without entering a PIN.

events.event: SSGC Managing Director Muhammad Amin Rajput stated that Pakistan's domestic gas output has halved over the last decade, forcing restricted supplies to domestic consumers during three daily meal times.
events.source_excerpt:
KARACHI: The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) has been forced to restrict supply to domestic consumers three meal times a day because of depleting indigenous production over the past decade, its managing director said on Saturday.
According to Muhammad Amin Rajput, the schedule was necessary as the country’s gas production had fallen about 50 per cent over the last decade, while imported LNG supplies, too, were hard to come by since April due to the Iran war.
“By focusing on supply during cooking hours, the company can protect domestic consumers,” the managing director said in an exclusive interview with Dawn.
He said SSGC’s gas availability had fallen to around 605 million cubic feet per day due to depletion in gas fields, compared with 695mmcfd last year. “Of this, around 300mmcfd is being given to domestic consumers, while the rest is supplied to industry, power and fertiliser sectors,” Mr Rajput added.

events.event: Gold prices in Pakistan fell by Rs. 700 per tola, extending a three-day total loss to Rs. 16,500.
events.source_excerpt:
Gold prices in Pakistan fell for a third straight day on Saturday, with 24-karat gold dropping by Rs. 700 to Rs. 410,936 per tola.
According to rates shared by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA), 10-gram gold also fell by Rs. 600 to Rs. 352,311.
Rs. 16,500 Lost in Three Days
Saturday’s dip was smaller than the previous two days, but it extended the slide. Gold fell by Rs. 10,900 per tola on Thursday and by Rs. 4,900 on Friday, as ProPakistani reported when gold lost nearly Rs. 16,000 in two days.
In total, gold has now shed Rs. 16,500 per tola in three days, down from Rs. 427,436 on Wednesday.
International Gold and Silver
The local decline followed the global market, where gold fell by $7 to $3,884 per ounce.
Silver also lost ground, falling by Rs. 124 to Rs. 5,343 per tola.
What This Means for Buyers
At Saturday’s rate:
- Half a tola of 24-karat gold costs about Rs. 205,468.
- One tola costs Rs. 410,936.
- Two tolas cost about Rs. 821,872, around Rs. 33,000 less than on Wednesday.
These are APGJSA rates for pure 24-karat gold; jewellery buyers also pay making charges on top.

The prison’s CCTV cameras are also being integrated with the Safe City system to strengthen surveillance and facilitate the real-time sharing of information about inmates.

events.event: US President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Washington floated a proposal for Ukraine to cede parts of the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership.
events.source_excerpt:
KYIV: Washington suggested Kyiv cede land to Moscow in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in comments released on Saturday, saying his country’s relationship with the Western alliance is “back on the agenda.”
Zelensky also warned of the dangers of Moscow’s push to redraw “influence” in Europe and said the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign. Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Putin and Zelensky on Thursday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough. Negotiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries join future talks on ending the war.
In Dublin on Friday, Europe chose five countries — France, Germany, Italy, the UK and Poland — to send representatives to the talks. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky said, adding: “After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go.” He believed “Nato is back on the agenda” as Ukraine — with almost five years of combat experience — can make the alliance “stronger.” Nato and Washington have not yet commented.
Kyiv seeks guarantees
Kyiv — seeking post-war support for its army — was in talks on “specific” guarantees from Western countries, Zelensky said. Before agreeing to anything, he added, he would ask Ukrainians “do we accept it or not?”. He insisted Ukraine would not recognise any land seized by Moscow’s troops as Russian.
