events.event: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi suspended all gold mining across the province and cancelled all mining leases as part of a crackdown on illegal mining.
events.source_excerpt:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has suspended all gold mining across the province and announced the cancellation of all gold mining leases, a month after he invited foreign companies to invest in the province’s minerals.
Speaking at a press conference in Peshawar on Saturday, Kundi said the decision was part of a crackdown on illegal mining, which he said was funding terrorism.
One-Week Deadline for Machinery
The governor ordered leaseholders and contractors to remove heavy machinery from mining areas within a week, warning that any machinery left after that would be seized.
He said fines would now be imposed in line with the law, instead of the small Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 30,000 penalties magistrates had been charging.
Kundi said illegal mining in Kohat’s Blocks C and D involved some 8,350 trucks, 3,660 excavators, 1,600 dumpers and around 50,000 labourers, with about 90 kilograms of gold being extracted every month.
He claimed 80 percent of the profits were sent to Afghanistan and used for terrorism.
Kohat Attack and Task Force
The move follows an attack in Kohat in which a DSP and 10 police personnel were martyred while returning from an operation against illegal mining.
Kundi named 12 politicians as allegedly backing illegal mining. He also announced a judicial commission headed by a retired Peshawar High Court judge and a task force named after martyred DSP Haider Zaman to draft a new mining strategy within three weeks.
From Investment Pitch to Ban
The ban comes after Kundi invited foreign companies for mineral joint ventures in October, and repeated the pitch at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad on Thursday, promising investors a one-window facility.

events.event: Leaders of the US, China, and Russia are scheduled to hold their first-ever trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on November 19 on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
events.source_excerpt:
The leaders of the United States, China and Russia will hold their first-ever three-way meeting on November 19 in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, RT reported.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the plan, saying, “An agreement has been reached to hold a trilateral meeting on the 19th between President Putin, Chairman Xi and President Trump.”
The APEC summit is scheduled for November 18-19 in Shenzhen and will bring together leaders of 21 Asia-Pacific economies.
What Is on the Table
Nuclear arms control and the situation around Iran are reportedly the main topics planned for discussion. Trump has said talks in this format are needed mainly to discuss nuclear disarmament.
The meeting would bring together the heads of the world’s three biggest nuclear powers at one table for the first time.
How the Summit Came Together
Trump said on November 8 that he expected to meet Putin and Xi at the summit. China’s Foreign Ministry had confirmed on November 6 that discussions on such a meeting were under way.
Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said last month that preparations had begun and that Moscow, Beijing and Washington were ready in principle to hold the talks. He added that Russia and the US had not agreed on a separate one-on-one meeting between Putin and Trump on the sidelines.
Not everyone is comfortable with the plan. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said many European leaders fear that Trump and Putin’s talks in China could turn into a “second Anchorage”, a reference to their earlier summit in Alaska.

United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry.
The Vulcan rocket is on contract to launch roughly half of the US military’s national security space missions in the next few years, and Sunday’s mission was the first of 38 Vulcan launches booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX’s Starlink. Sunday’s failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time.

events.source_excerpt:
Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
- Published
Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed on Sunday as the US air-traffic control system continued to recover from a technical failure that led to a rare national ground stop.
Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said normal operations may not be restored until Monday.
"We have airplanes and crews that are out of position, so it takes a little bit of time," he told the BBC's US partner CBS. More than 8,800 flights were delayed and 2,400 cancelled on Sunday.
President Donald Trump urged Congress on Sunday to approve more money to modernise the air-traffic control system. The grounding of all aircraft scheduled to depart the US on Friday caused chaos at airports across the country.
More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air when the FAA announced at 15:54 EST (20:54 GMT) that flights would be grounded until further notice. Some were diverted to other airports and others flew on to their destinations.
In the aftermath, 8,500 flights were delayed and another 8,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware.
The stoppage left passengers stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to their gates. Others were stranded in airports, sleeping on the floor and desperately trying to get in touch with their airline. The ground stop also had a knock-on effect on schedules around the world, with some flights out of the UK and Europe cancelled.
The ground stop was lifted after about four and a half hours, but the impacts continued over the weekend.
On Saturday, airlines cancelled more than 5,900 flights and more than 7,000 others were delayed.

events.event: A UN Food and Agriculture Organisation report warns that Punjab's water demand exceeds supply, with groundwater depleting by 5.5 billion cubic metres annually.
events.source_excerpt:
• FAO report says province losing 5.5bn cubic metres of groundwater annually 
• Highlights growing need for water resource management 
• Recommends setting up commission to review policies, existing strategies
• Identifies shortcomings in data collection, info consolidation
ISLAMABAD: A detailed assessment of Punjab’s water resources by a United Nations specialised agency has warned of serious challenges ahead, saying the province’s water demand already exceeds supply across all sectors.
The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said groundwater was being depleted by about 5.5 billion cubic metres annually over a five-year period, while surface water resources were also under growing pressure.
To assess the province’s water stress, the FAO sought expert advice from water specialists, including former Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) chairman Shamsul Mulk and former Indus River System Authority (Irsa) chairman Rao Irshad Ali Khan.
The findings, published in a report titled Water and Land Accounting in Punjab, were based on annual water accounts covering five water years from 2012 to 2017. The report highlighted the growing need for comprehensive water resources management, saying Punjab required more advanced and integrated water services across different sectors and regions.
It strongly recommended the establishment of a commission to conduct a one-time review of provincial water resources, water-related policies, institutional mandates and existing strategies.
The commission’s tasks would include ensuring coherence between national and inter-provincial policies and water initiatives, and establishing an integrated mechanism to assess the impact of transboundary water projects and other interventions.
